findings.claim: error-invalid-multivalued-size was rewritten from i18next placeholders ({{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}) to Java MessageFormat ({0}/{1}/{2} plus {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}). i18next does not interpolate single-brace placeholders and has no choice syntax, so the admin console shows the raw template. The change is also unrelated to HTML sanitising, and it forced a special case into VerifyMessageProperties.java:124.
findings.evidence: admin-ui src/i18n/i18n.ts uses default i18next with no ICU plugin. ThemeResource serves values raw, with no {n}->{{n}} conversion. ui-shared user-profile/utils.ts:74-85 calls t(key,{0,1,2}). Every sibling error-* key and every community translation of this key still use {{N}}. Superpowers gives a grep (single-brace or choice) that shows this key is the only such hit in admin-ui. All three seats call it reasoned; it was not run in a UI.
findings.reason: Three seats agree, and the evidence (i18n config, call site, sibling keys) is consistent across them. Before the fix, write a red test: an i18next unit test where t('error-invalid-multivalued-size',{0:'a',1:1,2:2}) returns the literal '{0}' text. The fix is to revert to {{n}}. The server-side base-theme change is correct and stays.

verifier.reason: The patch changes messages_en.properties:3138 from {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to MessageFormat {0}/{1}/{2} plus {2,choice,...}. The admin UI uses plain i18next with no ICU plugin and default {{ }} interpolation (js/apps/admin-ui/src/i18n/i18n.ts:13-34), and ThemeResource.java:141-143 serves the values unchanged, so t() in ui-shared/src/user-profile/utils.ts:79-85 shows the raw placeholders and the choice text. The patch also adds a special case for this key in VerifyMessageProperties.java to work around the '<' in the choice text.

findings.claim: This is the same {{N}} -> {N}/choice rewrite of error-invalid-multivalued-size, in the account console bundle. i18next will render the template literally.
findings.evidence: account-ui src/i18n.ts:27 uses default i18next delimiters and has no i18next-icu dependency. The call path through ui-shared setUserProfileServerError is the same as in admin-ui. Community translations (fr, pl and others) keep {{0}}. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. The red test is the same as for the admin-ui entry: an i18next interpolation test against the account-ui bundle. The fix is to revert to {{n}}.

verifier.reason: The patch changes account-ui messages_en.properties:188 to use `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` syntax. But account-ui/src/i18n.ts:25-43 sets up plain i18next with the default `{{ }}` delimiters, and package.json has no ICU plugin. ThemeResource.getLocalizationTexts (ThemeResource.java:121-154) sends the raw property values, and ui-shared setUserProfileServerError (utils.ts:64-89) passes them to t() unchanged, so the placeholders and the choice block appear literally.

findings.claim: The 'Didn't find anchor tag … in original string' error omits the key and the file, so a build failure across ~160-180 bundles cannot be located.
findings.evidence: Line 157 differs from the 'Illegal HTML' message at :111 and the error at :194, both of which name the file and key.

verifier.reason: VerifyMessageProperties.java:157 builds its message from only the anchor tag (`"Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string"`). It leaves out `key`, even though `key` is passed into santizeAnchors (:150), and it leaves out `file`. ThemeVerifierMojo.java:51-55 then merges every file's messages into one list without adding any file context, unlike the messages at :111 and :194, which name the key and/or the file.

findings.claim: Read failures in verifySafeHtml (:70, :79) throw a raw RuntimeException instead of the MojoExecutionException that verify() uses. The English sibling path is derived by replaceAll on the absolute path (:74-75), so a bundle with no _en twin crashes the mojo instead of reporting a validation error.
findings.evidence: verify() wraps IOException in MojoExecutionException at :52-53. The old duplicate_keys fixture had to be renamed because of this. Superpowers checked all 162 current bundles and every one resolves to an _en file, so nothing breaks today. Ponytail notes that the file is also re-read even though its contents are already in memory (L49).
findings.reason: Four seats agree. It is latent rather than live (all current bundles resolve), so Minor. The fix is to let IOException propagate (or wrap it in MojoExecutionException) and to report a missing _en file as a validation message.

verifier.reason: VerifyMessageProperties.java:70 and :79 wrap read failures in a raw RuntimeException, while verify() at :52-53 uses MojoExecutionException. The English file path comes from replaceAll on the absolute path (:74-75), so a bundle with no _en sibling crashes with an unchecked exception instead of producing a clean mojo error. This is why the patch renamed duplicate_keys.properties to duplicateKeys_en.properties.

findings.claim: The owasp-java-html-sanitizer version 20240325.1 is hard-coded and duplicates the root pom.xml:119 owasp.html.sanitizer.version property, so the two can drift.
findings.evidence: pom.xml:75-85 compared with root pom.xml:119/559. Mattpocock, superpowers and ponytail all note that the module is standalone with no parent and already hard-codes commons-io the same way.
findings.reason: The drift risk is real and no report disproves it. But open-code-review's proposed fix (use ${owasp.html.sanitizer.version} / root dependencyManagement) cannot work, because the module has no parent, as three seats state. The convention matches the module's existing commons-io pin. Defer with a comment at the dependency: 'ponytail: standalone module, no parent; keep in sync with root owasp.html.sanitizer.version'.

verifier.reason: The patch adds owasp-java-html-sanitizer with the version hard-coded as 20240325.1 at misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml:78, the same value as the owasp.html.sanitizer.version property at root pom.xml:119 (used at lines 561-571), so the two can drift. The module has no parent, so it cannot inherit the property, and commons-io is already hard-coded the same way at line 61; this makes the duplication a minor upkeep issue, not a bug.

findings.claim: The common-prefix/suffix trim used to build the 'Illegal HTML' message (:96-111) never caps start+end at the shorter length. When they overlap, sanitized.substring(start, length-end) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The verifier then crashes with a stack trace and stops checking the remaining keys and files, on exactly the bad input it exists to report.
findings.evidence:
There are two independent jshell repros of the verbatim trim logic. open-code-review: value 'x' -> Range [8, 4) out of bounds (diffcrash.jsh). ponytail: value 'Next ->
' -> Range [7, 6) out of bounds (trim.jsh). Both hardcode the sanitizer output rather than running OWASP end to end.
findings.reason: Two seats raised it, so it goes to the appendix and is not fixed under step 4. This is the strongest appendix item: an Important correctness claim with executed repros of the logic. The exact check that would settle it is a unit test feeding 'x' through the real sanitizer in VerifyMessageProperties. It should be considered for promotion.
